concepts.title: Properties of Acids and Bases
concepts.definition: Acids are substances that taste sour and have an acidic chemical nature, while bases are substances that taste bitter, feel soapy to the touch, and have a basic chemical nature.
concepts.key_idea: Acids are indeed sour; bases are both bitter and soapy.
question_patterns: what are the characteristics of acids
how do bases feel when touched
identify the nature of a substance based on taste
distinguish between acidic and basic substances
justify why properties of acids and bases matters

solution_steps.explain: Acids taste sour; bases taste bitter and feel soapy.

solution_steps.action: Classify the substance by its chemical nature
solution_steps.explain: A sour taste indicates an acidic nature, while a bitter and soapy feel indicates a basic nature.

solution_steps.action: Verify with an indicator if tasting is unsafe
solution_steps.explain: Use litmus or turmeric to confirm the classification without relying on taste alone.

concepts.title: Indicators
concepts.definition: Indicators are special substances that change their color when exposed to acidic or basic solutions, allowing us to identify their chemical nature without tasting them.
concepts.key_idea: Indicators signal acidity or basicity through color change.
question_patterns: how do indicators help identify substances
what happens to litmus in an acidic solution
state two key points about indicators

solution_steps.explain: Litmus turns red in acid and blue in base.
Natural indicators like litmus, turmeric, or china rose petals reveal whether a solution is acidic or basic through a distinct color change.
The observed color confirms the chemical nature of the solution without tasting it.

concepts.title: Neutralisation Reaction
concepts.definition: Neutralisation is a chemical process where an acid and a base react to form both salt and water, releasing heat in the process.
concepts.key_idea: Acid and base cancel each other's effects to create both salt and water.
question_patterns: what are the products of a neutralisation reaction
calculate the outcome of mixing acid and base
describe neutralisation reaction with an example

solution_steps.explain: Acid and base are mixed in suitable amounts.
Heat is evolved during the reaction.
The reaction produces a salt and water, which are the characteristic products of neutralisation.

solution_template.explain: Neutralisation occurs between HCl and NaOH.
The reaction produces sodium chloride (salt) and water.
